title.purpose: Function name or Overview at the top of each column.

summary.purpose: One-paragraph function or project summary, max 60ch, in Soft Ink.

body.purpose: Page default; walkthrough step titles at weight 600.

body-sm.purpose: Entry-point text, walkthrough steps and notes in the overview, max 60ch.

ui.purpose: Header, breadcrumb, Find and Files, filter field, outdated note.

label.purpose: Sentence-case section heads (Calls, Called by, Where to start) in Grey Text.

meta.purpose: File location, sidebar file groups, line counts with tabular figures.

code.purpose: Pseudocode blocks. Ligatures off (font-variant-ligatures: none). Wrapped lines hang under their own indentation.

identifier.purpose: Function names in lists and chains. Weight 600 marks the open one. Ligatures off.

shadows.name: hollow-dot-ring
shadows.purpose: Draws the hollow 'not described' status dot. It is a stroke, not elevation. The system has no elevation shadows.

motion.name: ease-enter
motion.purpose: The only custom easing (--ease). Used when a new column enters.

motion.name: column-enter
motion.purpose: A newly opened column eases in from the right. Removed under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: control-fade
motion.purpose: Column controls fade in on column hover or focus-within.

motion.name: strip-scroll
motion.purpose: The strip scrolls to the first column edge that fits. Instant on first load and on back or forward.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: At or below: sidebar, Find and Files hidden; columns 88vw; header and strip padding reduced.

narrative.overview:
pseudoview is a reading page. A developer opens it to learn what a function does without reading the source. Type and space do all the work. Content has no cards, no panel borders, no header bar and no fills. Columns sit on one near-black ground and only space separates them. The pseudocode looks like a typed document, not an editor.

The page is dense and calm. Most text is 12 to 15px. There are two faces: system sans for prose and one mono for pseudocode and identifiers. The palette is grey. Two hues exist, and each one carries a single meaning. Blue means "described" and "the path you opened". Amber means "the code changed after this was written". Nothing else gets colour, and that includes the pseudocode. Keywords are bold ink and comments are grey.

Navigation is Finder-style. Opening a call adds a column on the right. The page itself never scrolls. Only the sidebar and each column scroll. The strip of columns always stops at a column's left edge, so no column shows cut through its text.
keyCharacteristics: One near-black ground with no surfaces on top of it.
Two faces: system sans for prose, mono for code and identifiers.
Colour means state. Blue is described or open, amber is outdated.
Status is a 6px dot, never a badge.
Links are underlined in a dark grey, and the open link's underline turns blue.
Columns are separated only by space, and controls stay hidden until hover.

rules.name: The Two Signals Rule
rules.body: Blue and amber are the only hues. Blue means described, open or focused. Amber means outdated. Do not use either for emphasis, branding or decoration, and do not add a third hue.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Hue Rule
rules.body: Pseudocode has no syntax colours. Keywords are Ink at weight 600, comments are Grey Text, and calls are underlined Ink. Everything else is Soft Ink.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Sans is for sentences. Mono is for code and for names that exist in code. Never set prose in mono or an identifier in sans.

rules.name: The No-Shouting Rule
rules.body: Labels are small, grey and sentence case. Hierarchy comes from size steps (12 to 20px) and weight (400, 500, 600), not from caps or tracking.

rules.name: The Still Page Rule
rules.body: The page itself never scrolls or shifts. Only the sidebar and the individual columns scroll.

rules.name: The Column Edge Rule
rules.body: When the strip moves, it stops at a column's left edge and shows the newest column plus as many parents as fit. Never leave a column cut through its text.

rules.name: The Flat Ground Rule
rules.body: Every element sits on the one ground. If something needs to stand out, give it weight, ink or a signal colour, never a shadow or a panel.

dos: **Do** put every element straight on the Ground (#0e0e0f). Separate columns and sections with space only.
**Do** use Soft Ink (#c9c9ce) for long reading text and Ink (#ececec) for names, keywords, links and active states.
**Do** keep Signal Blue (#5b8cff) for described, open and focused, and Outdated Amber (#e0a33a) for outdated. Nothing else.
**Do** show status with the 6px dot, and say outdated in words as well as in amber.
**Do** mark function links with an underline in Grey Line, 3px offset, and switch the open one to a 2px blue underline.
**Do** set pseudocode and identifiers in the mono at 12.5px with ligatures off, and prose in system sans.
**Do** honour reduced motion and show hidden controls on touch screens.
donts: **Don't** add cards, panels, borders, fills or shadows around content. The filter field's bottom rule and the icon button's hover wash are the only exceptions, and both belong to controls.
**Don't** colour pseudocode by syntax. Keywords get weight, comments get grey.
**Don't** use Grey Line (#4a4a50) for text a reader must read.
**Don't** add a header bar, a toolbar background or a divider between columns.
**Don't** let the page scroll, or let opening a column move anything to its left.
**Don't** use badges or pills for status or tags. Tags are plain text after " · ".
**Don't** set labels in uppercase or with wide tracking.
